authoredNote: Source written first from the #866 pre-declared contract (java/groovy already satisfied it; kotlin was measured to violate BOTH halves). The expectation was recorded from the post-fix run only to get the spelling of kind/owner and the exact call lines right — the contract itself is the issue's, not the run's.
rationale: M49/M37 #866: kotlin diverged from the family in two ways, both pinned here. (1) `val field` inside `object : Runnable { ... }` was dropped entirely — extractProperty's ancestor scan stopped only at class_declaration/object_declaration, so it walked PAST the object_literal, reached the enclosing function_declaration, and classified the member as a local. It is now a `property` symbol owned by anonymous_Runnable, matching java/groovy. (2) the initialiser's call was attributed to the OUTER method `build` (resolveCallSource had no object_literal boundary) while java/groovy/scala all say the anonymous type; the anon name now comes from the same derivation the symbol emitter uses, so the member symbol and its initialiser call cannot disagree. The `local` control pins the OTHER half of the same boundary: a method-local is not a project symbol. Call lines are pinned because the `local` call in build() is legitimately attributed to build.
